summary:
OrbitED is an interactive 3D educational web application that transforms space exploration into a hands-on learning experience. Developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge’s "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge, OrbitED introduces students to life on the Moon and Mars through three connected learning approaches: building, exploring, and completing missions.

Players can build their own planetary bases by selecting and placing structures, explore detailed 3D models and environments from different perspectives, and take on seven-day survival missions on the Moon or Mars. During these missions, they must think like engineers and astronauts, make decisions, solve problems, and understand how each choice affects their survival and available resources.

OrbitED is important because it moves space education beyond reading and observation. By combining interactive construction, immersive 3D exploration, and mission-based challenges, it encourages critical thinking, creativity, engineering skills, and problem-solving while making the challenges of living beyond Earth more engaging and accessible to students.
details:
Project Details – OrbitED

1. Project Overview

OrbitED is an interactive 3D educational web application designed to introduce students to the challenges of human space exploration and life beyond Earth. Developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge's "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge, OrbitED transforms space education from passive learning into an engaging, hands-on experience.

The project focuses on three connected learning approaches: Learning by Building, Learning by Exploring, and Learning through Missions. Together, these approaches allow learners to experience different aspects of establishing and surviving in a human settlement on the Moon or Mars.

2. How Does OrbitED Work?

A. Learning by Building

Players can design and build their own planetary bases by selecting different structures and placing them within the environment. They can interact with the building process, adjust the placement and orientation of structures, and deploy them as part of their base.

This approach introduces learners to the importance of planning, infrastructure, and engineering decisions when establishing a settlement beyond Earth.

B. Learning by Exploring – Interactive 3D Models

OrbitED provides interactive 3D environments and models that learners can explore from different perspectives. Instead of relying only on pictures or written descriptions, players can view and interact with planetary environments and structures, making space-related concepts easier to visualize and understand.

The experience covers both the Moon and Mars, allowing learners to explore two different environments and discover the challenges associated with each.

C. Learning through Missions – Seven-Day Survival Experience

OrbitED introduces mission-based learning through a simulated seven-day survival experience on the Moon or Mars.

Players take on the role of junior astronauts and must think like engineers when making decisions throughout their missions. Each decision can influence their survival conditions and available resources, encouraging them to consider consequences, evaluate options, and solve problems.

This approach helps learners understand that surviving beyond Earth requires more than building a base: it also requires planning, critical thinking, and making responsible decisions under challenging conditions.

3. Benefits and Educational Value

OrbitED provides several educational benefits:

  • Engineering Thinking: Encourages learners to approach challenges like engineers and consider practical solutions.
  • Critical Thinking: Helps players evaluate choices and understand their possible consequences.
  • Problem-Solving: Introduces challenges that require planning, experimentation, and decision-making.
  • Spatial Understanding: Makes planetary environments and structures easier to understand through interactive 3D visualization.
  • Creativity: Gives learners opportunities to build and organize their own planetary bases.
  • Active Learning: Encourages learning through exploration, interaction, and mission experiences rather than passive observation.

4. Intended Impact

OrbitED aims to make space education more accessible, engaging, and memorable, especially for students and young learners.

By combining interactive construction, 3D exploration, and survival missions, the project helps learners connect scientific and engineering concepts with practical experiences. It encourages curiosity about space exploration and inspires students to think about the technologies, decisions, and challenges involved in future human missions to the Moon and Mars.

Our goal is to help learners move beyond simply imagining life in space and give them an opportunity to experience some of its challenges through an interactive educational environment.

5. Technologies and Development Tools

The project was developed as a browser-based application using:

  • React.js: Building the frontend application and reusable interface components.
  • JavaScript: Implementing application logic and interactive functionality.
  • HTML5 and CSS3: Structuring and styling the application.
  • Tailwind CSS: Creating and styling the user interface.
  • Three.js: Rendering interactive 3D scenes and objects.
  • React Three Fiber: Integrating 3D environments and interactions into the React application.
  • GLB/glTF: Integrating 3D models and assets into the experience.
  • Git and GitHub: Managing source code and supporting team collaboration.
  • Vercel: Deploying and hosting the application for public access.

AI tools, including ChatGPT and Google Gemini Pro, were also used as supporting assistants for technical research, programming assistance, troubleshooting, and documentation. The team remained responsible for the project decisions, implementation, integration, and testing.

6. Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of OrbitED lies in combining three complementary educational experiences within one application.

Rather than presenting space exploration as a collection of static lessons, OrbitED gives learners different ways to engage with the subject: they can build a planetary base, explore its environment through interactive 3D models, and experience mission-based survival challenges.

Connecting these experiences creates a more immersive learning journey in which learners can move from understanding their environment to constructing within it and making decisions about survival.

7. Factors Considered During Development

While developing OrbitED, our team considered:

  • Educational Value: Making sure that interactions support learning about space exploration rather than serving only as entertainment.
  • User Experience: Designing an understandable and accessible journey for students and young learners.
  • Visual Clarity: Using interactive 3D environments to make complex space-related ideas easier to visualize.
  • Engagement: Combining building, exploration, and missions to maintain curiosity and active participation.
  • Technical Feasibility: Choosing browser-compatible technologies that support interactive 3D experiences.
  • Performance and Accessibility: Considering model loading, application responsiveness, and access through a web browser.
  • Future Expandability: Designing the experience with the potential to introduce additional environments, structures, and educational missions.

Through OrbitED, we aim to turn the challenges of living beyond Earth into an opportunity for students to explore, build, think, and learn by experience.
